kurz: A non-stick coating is so slick that protein can barely grip it. It is ideal for eggs and fish, but cannot take very high heat.
bild_im_kopf: Like water drops on a lotus leaf: nothing can get a hold.
was_passiert: Classic coatings are made of PTFE, a plastic that almost nothing sticks to. From about 260 °C it starts to break down and gives off fumes. An empty pan reaches that temperature on a strong flame or induction within minutes, but hardly ever with food in it. Ceramic coatings tolerate more heat but lose their slickness faster.
warum_wichtig: A dark crust on steak needs more heat than the coating likes. Knowing this, you use the right pan for each job, and the non-stick one lasts much longer.
faustregeln: For eggs, pancakes and fish: the non-stick pan, because protein doesn't stick to it.
For steak and hard searing: iron or stainless steel, because the crust needs more heat than the coating can take.
Replace it once the coating is scratched or everything sticks.
schritte: Put fat or food into the pan before heating, never heat it empty on high.
Use medium to medium-high heat at most.
Use wooden or silicone spatulas, not metal.
Let the pan cool down before it goes into water.
Wash it by hand with a soft sponge.

mythos.richtig: At normal cooking heat PTFE is stable. It only becomes a problem when overheated, typically in a pan heated empty.
